key_insight: Centrosymmetric solids can generate dc photocurrents through coupling between light’s electric and magnetic fields, without requiring broken spatial inversion symmetry.
engineering_relevance: The magnetoelectric bulk photovoltaic effect could expand candidate photovoltaic materials and enable electrical readout of altermagnetic order.
method: Connect photocurrents to dipole moments of the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature.
Classify four injection-like and shift-like mechanisms by time-reversal symmetry and light polarization.
Analyze symmetry constraints and predict responses in monolayer Pt₂HgSe₃ and altermagnetic RuF₄.
evidence_signal: The abstract predicts two-dimensional current densities on the order of 1 mA/m, with RuF₄ injection-like current reversing upon switching either light helicity or the Néel vector.
watch_item: The abstract reports theoretical predictions, not experimental validation or solar-cell conversion efficiency.
paper_title: Magnetoelectric Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in Centrosymmetric Solids
